proposal.summary: WorldServer (<= 11.7.3) uses low-entropy numeric session tokens (positive values below 2^31) that can be enumerated via the SOAP loginWithToken action, allowing attackers to discover and use valid session tokens including administrative sessions.
proposal.cwe_quote: WorldServer associates user sessions with numerical tokens, which always are positive values below 2^31.

AV.quote: The --range parameter reflects the possible value range of 2^31 and for each value an HTTP request is sent to the WorldServer SOAP API where the FUZZ marker in the request template is replaced with the respective value.

PR.quote: For each value an HTTP request is sent to the WorldServer SOAP API where the FUZZ marker in the request template is replaced with the respective value.

UI.quote: for each value an HTTP request is sent to the WorldServer SOAP API

C.quote: Responses will yield a status code of 200 if an administrative session token is found. For an unprivileged user session, status code 500 is returned.

I.quote: Attackers can efficiently enumerate session tokens. In a penetration test, it was possible to get access to multiple user accounts, including administrative accounts using this method in under three hours.

A.quote: Attackers can efficiently enumerate session tokens. In a penetration test, it was possible to get access to multiple user accounts, including administrative accounts using this method in under three hours.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Attempt to reproduce the token enumeration against a test instance: run the provided SOAP loginWithToken fuzzing request pattern to confirm token value distribution and whether administrative tokens are discoverable; capture request/response showing successful administrative login and any session contents.

evidence_quotes.quote: WorldServer associates user sessions with numerical tokens, which always are positive values below 2^31.

evidence_quotes.claim: Enumerability and low entropy (7-digit tokens observed)
evidence_quotes.quote: During analysis, many assigned tokens were found to be in the 7-digit range of values. An attacker is therefore able to enumerate user accounts in only a few hours.

evidence_quotes.claim: Vulnerable SOAP action and request example
evidence_quotes.quote: The SOAP action "loginWithToken" allows for a high amount of parallel attempts to check if a token is valid.

evidence_quotes.claim: Automated enumeration command example and throughput
Observations of successful responses and speed
evidence_quotes.quote:
processed 12000000 HTTP requests in 2h38m38s
4 of 12000000 requests shown, 1225 req/s
Responses will yield a status code of 200 if an administrative session token is found. For an unprivileged user session, status code 500 is returned.
In a penetration test, it was possible to get access to multiple user accounts, including administrative accounts using this method in under three hours.
According to the vendor, upgrading to versions above 11.8.0 resolves the vulnerability.
